pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented against his own stated constraint — that a rigid push/pull split collapses when his week shifts — with "with kettlebell training, each single workout, you're going to be working on strength, conditioning, and mobility... So if you miss one, that's no biggie", 30-40 minutes, three to four times a week, plus short daily mobility protocols and portability for RV trips and hotel gyms. One clarifying beat ("are like mobility stretches, right? Like the different movements, five minutes") then straight acceptance: "I think so. Yeah." and no questions.

Simple-rules framing — what you eat, when you eat, how much you eat, an eight-hour window, no calorie counting, one meal out a week. The prospect's only reaction was surprise at the diagnosis rather than pushback on the method: "Under-eating?" He then accepted it — "Yeah. Yeah." Notable that he had already told the rep he knows the science and has done the research, so the objection this pillar needed to answer was compliance, not knowledge, and that was not addressed here.

Presented as the most important pillar for him, and it drew every substantive question he asked all call — about Trevor's methods ("is that all he does is kettlebells and pull-ups and push-ups? I mean, he doesn't do gym, doesn't take anything else to help him, like medicine or drugs?"), supplements ("What about like protein shakes"), capacity ("How many people does he usually take per month"), and attrition ("do you have people that commit to it and they give up, they quit?"). He was buying the relationship, not the programming, and he was diligencing it. He tied it to his own gap unprompted: "this is the key, not to fall off like we did before."

anchors.raw: usually it is an investment i was maybe thinking it was going to be between five six hundred dollars a month kind of deal i mean even a thousand dollars a month but it is like you're up fronting
anchors.note: The anchor is monthly, not total. At $1,000 a month his expectation would have reached $6,000 over six months — the objection was almost entirely to the lump-sum shape rather than to the number. Restated even more explicitly at 00:53:37: "if you're telling me today, hey, you can [do a] thousand down or we're gonna start doing 600 bucks a month or whatever, like, ah, let's do it. But it's, it's, you know, 6,000." A payment structure, not a discount, was what this deal needed.

anchors.raw: this is all new to me, right? I've never even done a personal trainer. I've never done a coaching before. This is my first time ever approaching anybody for coaching or doing anything online.
anchors.note: He has no prior coaching purchase to price against, so $6,000 was evaluated against nothing. That absence — rather than a competitor — is what made the number feel large, and it is the case where anchoring the offer against the cost of the problem would have done the most work.

anchors.raw: things that I've learned with my business is, you know, not to reinvent the wheel. And, you know, I just want something that, uh, to save time and I don't want to continue, uh, just trying to push it, you know, and not see the results.
anchors.note: He is habituated to paying for systems rather than building them, and said so in his first ninety seconds. The strongest supportive anchor on the call and the rep used it well early — "That's definitely a businessman approach to save time."

anchors.raw: there's been a lot of, I've seen other training, other people, you know, offering stuff on social media, I never felt engaged to like, ah, you know, to do it. right this was kind of the first time that i felt engaged to actually do set this up because it's because of trevor because he's a genuine dude
anchors.note: The purchase is anchored on Trevor personally, not on the programme or the modality. He found him on YouTube, subscribed and booked the same day. Worth knowing that the perceived product here is access to a specific person.

anchors.raw: What Trevor does is guaranteeing that in those six months, you will add eight kilos, which is around like 17 pounds, 17, 18 pounds, to your baseline weight of kettlebell that you start with, to all the basic movements. If you, if you wouldn't, for some reason, hit that, he will work for you until you do for free.
anchors.note: Deployed to answer risk and it worked, but it guarantees strength progression while his stated goal is body composition. The gap was never noticed by either party.

unmet_demand.want: A smaller first commitment — a way to try coaching before committing $6,000, having never bought coaching before
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The stated offer has no trial and no entry tier. The rep manufactured one live: "let's settle on 1200 for a month you get in Trevor will map out the whole program for you... you will work with him for a month and then after one month you will decide whether you want to continue." That structure is not part of the offer and its terms were improvised.

unmet_demand.want: A guarantee tied to the outcome he actually came for — getting leaner and dropping body fat
unmet_demand.why_unmet: What is guaranteed is strength: about 8 kg added to his baseline kettlebell weight across the basic movements within six months. Nothing about body composition is guaranteed, and the substitution passed unremarked. He accepted a strength promise as security for a fat-loss purchase.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that an eight-year-old, never-assessed wrist injury will hold up under loaded kettlebell work
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with a mechanical reassurance about press angles — "the cool thing with kettlebells even when you do the presses it's not like with a barbell that the wrist is you know right angle" — rather than any screening or clearance step, because none exists in the offer. The same gap the ICP file already identifies: there is no clinical criterion anywhere in the process.

unmet_demand.want: Monthly billing rather than an upfront lump sum
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Available, but priced as a penalty — six installments at $1,200 carries $1,200 of additional cost — and then partly abandoned in the improvised structure. He said plainly that monthly at his number would have been an instant yes.
